scores.evidence: Phase 0 Discovery ... build the golden set, pick the stack; Phase 1 Prototype: Ingestion, hybrid retrieval, prompt, offline eval harness
scores.rationale: Rollout roughly goes discovery→ingestion/retrieval→agent assist→beta, but it is a product-rollout sequence and not a substrate-up dependency ordering with proven gates.
Phase 0 is discovery and there is no thin end-to-end slice in production first; the first real deployment comes only at beta.

scores.evidence: Use pgvector if you already run Postgres. Otherwise use a managed vector database
scores.rationale: Some defaults with conditions exist (vector store, model tier, embeddings), but there is no consolidated irreversible-decision list with explicit flip conditions.
No ordering of work by blast radius within phases is stated.

scores.evidence: Visibility filter at index time *and* at query time
scores.rationale: Security is covered in standalone guardrails/risk sections (PII, rate limits, injection) but not tied to each rollout phase.

scores.evidence: trace every turn (query, rewrite, retrieved IDs, scores, prompt version, model, latency, cost)
scores.rationale: Observability is detailed but in a standalone operations section, not in Phase 0 and each phase; dashboards show up only at GA.

scores.evidence: version prompts, the index and the embedding model, and be able to roll back.
scores.rationale: Versioning and blue/green indexes are mentioned, and CI evals run on changes, but reproducibility is not threaded per phase.

scores.evidence: nightly full sync to catch anything missed
scores.rationale: Failure handling such as escalation, fallback sync and refusal exists but is scattered and not phased; nothing covers provider outages or timeouts.

scores.evidence: Build a golden dataset before tuning anything
scores.rationale: The plan has guardrails, cost caps, human handoff and retrieval→generation→feedback, but these are described as architecture rather than sequenced defenses-first. Budgets are late and the rollout puts the prototype before guardrails. Memory and orchestration are barely treated.

scores.evidence: Out of scope for v1: account-specific actions such as refunds, order lookup or password resets. Plan for these as tool calls in v2.
scores.rationale: Deferred items are named (v2 tool calls, proactive suggestions), but there is no explicit pull-forward condition.

note: This is a solid, practical RAG design, but it isn't ordered as a build plan: it has no production walking skeleton, no blast-radius ordering, and security, observability and resilience aren't threaded through the phases.
